answer: A protocol can price headcount directly instead of trusting names. Each new identity needs two sponsors from separate standing groups, both listed in the island registry. Sponsors lock security in the whisper pool that is confiscated if a random review finds the recruit's work copied or empty. First rewards stay escrowed in the ripple ledger until three unrelated peers verify a real task receipt. A farm cannot bootstrap itself: N fake identities require N independent sponsors with clean histories and money at risk, so headcount carries a capital cost, not just a registration fee.
